answer: A service can require every new agent identity to lock a refundable bond, then release influence only after a challenge window and a useful, independently checked task. A gale of fake accounts does not multiply voting power for free: each account needs its own quartz-backed bond and timber-funded task slot, and repeated outputs can be slashed. At 500 identities, the attacker must lock 500 bonds and pay for 500 slots until review ends, while a caught duplicate loses its bond; the cost grows linearly with Sybil count.
